Summary

Feedback loop: government needs private buyers for debt at affordable yields; the same system uses that debt as collateral. Rising yields raise financing costs, hurt bond books, shrink warehouse capacity, and force more issuance for interest — undermining absorption. Political path of least resistance is making gov debt easier to hold (bills, regs, stablecoin reserves, backstops, possible renewed CB buys) rather than tax hikes or spending cuts. Financial repression can start before announced QE; QE that swaps fixed for floating-rate exposure can leave fiscal arithmetic unresolved while staking dollar purchasing-power credibility.
